newsitem.title: ESTONIA: Estonian shares take breather after record week.
newsitem.headline: Estonian shares take breather after record week.

text.p: Estonian shares saw a small correction by Friday's close after a week of setting records as leading shares Hansapank and Hoiupank slipped.
Dealers said the market was now looking forward to the release of banks' consolidated group results next week.
The banks have so far given results for only their banking activities and figures from leasing and asset management operations are expected to give them a further boost.
Total trade on the main list was 74.4 million kroons with the Talse index 1.62 percent lower at 305.43.
"For next week, we do not expect any major falls with group results due out," one dealer said.
"Prices should hold around this level on what should be a generally a slow week," he added.

The bourse opened with some selling pressure and stocks moved down but Helsinki again helped Hansapank, where it is also quoted. But the Finnish buying ran out of steam leading to a fall of 4.25 kroons to 171.25 for the market leader on trade of 27.2 million kroons.
Hoiupank shadowed Hansapank and also eased to close on 172.50 kroons, 1.5 kroons lower on trade of 14.4 million kroons.
On the free market interest in Norma continued with 6.5 million kroons traded to rise in price.
The automotive safety belt manufacturer was 1.50 kroons higher at 80.00 kroons.
